title: Max Every Skills: my Roblox skilling RPG, with AI across code, visuals, audio and text
author: Elliotest
selftext:
I've always wanted to make a game, but I didn't have the technical skills to build one on my own. Max Every Skills is the project I finally brought to Roblox: a fantasy RPG with 15 skills, gathering, crafting, combat and rebirth progression. Eligible activities also keep progressing while you're away.



My imagination, ideas and creative vision are my own. I relied on generative AI throughout the implementation, including code, visuals, audio and text. This post is also written with AI assistance. I want to be clear about that rather than present the project as something I coded or drew by hand.



One concrete design question I'd like to discuss here is how to evaluate the whole progression loop when using AI across so many systems. Gathering, crafting and rebirths can each work individually, but that doesn't automatically mean they make a satisfying game together. For people who have developed games this way, how do you test that the systems fit together? Player feedback on the first few minutes and the pacing of skill progression would be especially useful to me.



I've put my heart into this project, am regularly improving it, and want to take players' feedback into account. The game page includes a roughly 49-second video of actual recorded gameplay, not an AI-generated video; the game shown still uses AI-created content. You can find it here: [https://www.roblox.com/games/97002479703204/Max-Every-Skills](https://www.roblox.com/games/97002479703204/Max-Every-Skills)
